requirement:
`OutlineItem::span` covers the item and every attachment it owns, including
leading and trailing attachments. Selecting the item returns the contiguous
source slice covered by that span.
rationale:
structural: Every clause of `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.item_span` states observable behavior. It prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation.

- "`OutlineItem::span` covers the item and every attachment it owns, including leading and trailing attachments" constrains the value of `span`. Any construction that yields the same offsets satisfies it. For example, an outline builder could compute the span either by extending it over attachments after the fact or by measuring them first. Both produce the same result, so the choice is discretionary.
- "Selecting the item returns the contiguous source slice covered by that span" constrains what selection returns. It does not say how selection is wired.

The `span: Span` field is declared by the parent requirement `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`, not by this subject's text. It is implemented at `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/contents.rs#struct[OutlineItem]`, which also documents that `span` includes every owned attachment. This subject adds no structural obligation beyond that declaration.

No implementation roots were supplied, and none is needed. Whether the value is correct is a behavioral question for the behavioral criterion.

behavioral: The requirement has two behavioral obligations: (1) `OutlineItem::span` covers the item and every attachment it owns, leading and trailing, and (2) selecting the item returns the contiguous source slice for that span. The reviewed tests cover both.

- `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_in_leading_and_trailing_comments_selects_the_function]` uses Rust source with a leading comment and a trailing comment. It asserts that selecting `fn[check]` returns exactly `// note before\npub fn check() {} // note after`. That shows both attachment kinds are inside the selected slice and that the slice is contiguous. It also asserts that `header_span` stays on the function header, and that the structural hash ignores the comment text.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[yaml_selection_includes_comments_owned_by_the_entry]` covers a trailing comment on a pair. It asserts that the outline item's `span` equals `Span::new(0, text.len())` and that `selected.text()` equals the slice. It also covers leading comments on sequence items and on a pair after a nested mapping, where a comment belongs to the following entry. Each case asserts the exact selected text, including that the preceding sibling's span excludes the comment.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[python_selected_source_includes_its_decorators]` covers leading decorator attachments. It asserts that the selected text equals the whole decorated source, that the item's span starts at 0, and that duplicate-named classes each start with their own decorator.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[custom_attachment_spans_are_checked_against_the_original_snapshot]` covers the span boundary. It uses a custom language and rejects an attachment that extends past its item (`Span::new(1, 4)` is an error). It accepts attachments inside the item and checks the attachment text against the snapshot. This shows the item span acts as the attachment container.

The tests cover leading and trailing attachments, several languages, and the selected-text assertion, so I found no uncovered obligation. I did not request implementation source.

`selector` addresses the item and `kind` describes it. `span` locates the whole item under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.Span`.
`structural_hash` identifies the item’s outline-relevant contents. A language supplies the digest excluding descendants with `with_own_hash` when it differs from the structural hash.
`attachments` lists the source constructs assigned to this item under
the list to empty. `with_attachments` sets it to the supplied list.
pub fn with_name_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_header_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_trailer_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_own_hash(self, hash: String) -> Self;
pub fn with_attachments(self, attachments: Vec<OutlineAttachment>) -> Self;
